grading_notes: Grade each assertion strictly and on its own. It passes only if the response states the specific point; a neighbouring or more general point does not count.

Credit equivalent wording. An assertion tests a behaviour, not the skill's vocabulary: "check it does not flag a correct page" is a control case, "break it on purpose and confirm it fails" is a break-test.
Credit an assertion wherever the point appears (main findings, a side note, a table row), but not if it is only implied by a code snippet the response never explains.
Ignore tone, format, length and house style. Ignore any locale, audience or timezone the response assumes; that comes from the environment the run happened in, not from the prompt.

evals.prompt: Our SEO agency sent us this audit (evals/fixtures/audit-report.md) for our website, whose built files are in evals/fixtures/site/dist (the repo README is at evals/fixtures/site/README.md). Which of their recommendations should we act on, and is there anything important they missed?
evals.expected_output: Measures each claim against the built files rather than trusting it. Rejects the false claims (logo alt is correct beside the visible name, Organization JSON-LD is present, the sitemap lists a page that does not exist and uses the build time as lastmod, the about page's h1 is styled smaller than its h2) and the harmful ones (lazy on the first hero and on display:none slides, more autoplay on a carousel that already autoplays). Confirms the title is too long but measures it in pixels and notices the audit's character count is wrong. Finds what the homepage-only crawl missed: disabled zoom, the Formspree id in HTML with no server-side bot verification, the rcm= share parameter, personal data on the about page, dead links, the trailing-slash mismatch between canonical and sitemap, a 13px input, ungated hover, and partner marks uppercased by CSS. Places each check in a gate, with must-hold checks in the build because CI runs alongside the deploy, and says what a session cannot verify.
assertions: Rejects the logo alt claim because the visible company name sits beside the logo inside the same link, so alt="" is correct
Rejects the structured data claim: Organization JSON-LD is already present on the homepage
Measures the homepage title in pixels (states a pixel width, or measures it against a roughly 600px desktop limit) rather than only counting characters
Counts the title itself and notices it does not match the audit's 97 characters (it is 91)
Says the first (visible) hero image should load eagerly rather than lazily
Identifies that loading="lazy" on display:none carousel slides interacts badly (the hidden images have no box, so they load only when shown, late, or not at all)
Rejects adding autoplay because the carousel already auto-advances every 4 seconds
Flags the missing pause control on the auto-advancing carousel, citing WCAG 2.2.2 (Pause, Stop, Hide)
Says the carousel must not auto-advance under prefers-reduced-motion
Rejects the sitemap claim because it lists /pricing/, which does not exist in the build
Rejects the sitemap claim because lastmod is the build timestamp, which changes every deploy, rather than the date the page content changed
Flags the trailing-slash mismatch between the about page's canonical (/about) and the sitemap and nav (/about/)
Rejects the heading claim because the about page's h1 is styled as a small heading under a bigger-styled h2 (or otherwise identifies a heading-hierarchy problem the audit called excellent)
Flags that the viewport meta disables zoom (maximum-scale=1 and/or user-scalable=no)
Flags the Formspree form id exposed in the built HTML as something to move server-side or into a secret
Says bot protection must be verified on the server (token verification, honeypot or similar), not only in the browser
Flags the rcm= parameter on the LinkedIn link as identifying the person who shared it, and says to strip the query string
Flags the named lab manager and mobile number on the about page as personal data that should not be published
Flags dead internal links (/pricing and/or /services/*)
Flags the 13px email input (iOS zooms on focus below 16px)
Flags the card hover lift as ungated (should sit inside @media (hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))
Flags text-transform: uppercase on the partner line as destroying partner brand casing (pH-Metrix, eZyCal)
Notes that the audit crawled only the homepage, and audits the about page itself
Says must-hold checks (personal data, leaks) belong in the build/postbuild step because the host deploys on push while CI runs in parallel and cannot stop it
Assigns a gate to each proposed check (build/postbuild vs CI static vs browser sweep vs live vs device), not just for one or two findings
Names at least one thing it could not verify from built files or an agent session (touch feel, real lazy-loading behaviour, live headers) and how a person should check it

evals.prompt: We are about to build a small microsite for a professional training programme: about 8 pages, a news section the programme coordinator will update through a git-based CMS, an enquiry form, and an embedded YouTube video on the home page. It will be Astro on Cloudflare, deployed automatically on every push. Before anyone builds pages, what should we set up and decide?
evals.expected_output: A day-one plan: what a push deploys and which gate can stop it; check scaffolding split across postbuild, CI static, browser sweep and live checks, each break-tested with a control; CSP without unsafe-inline and the Astro inline-script problem; a server-side form handler that verifies the bot token and is tested with a forged token, with the endpoint id in a secret; click-to-load video; CMS schema parity in both directions, report-vs-fail, and pasted-link rules; URL form, duplicate origins off, 404 with a 404 status, immutable assets; title budgets in pixels; house profile, ledger, and a mobile and motion baseline.
assertions: Says to find out what a push deploys (for example that a push to any branch may deploy) before relying on it
Says only the host's build step can block a deploy, and that CI runs alongside it and cannot
Places specific checks in specific gates (for example leaks and house style at postbuild; links and meta in CI; layout in a browser sweep; headers checked live)
Says every check should be break-tested: broken on purpose and seen to fail before it is trusted
Says each check needs a control case: a nearby input that must not fire
Says the form must verify the bot-check token on the server (not rely on a client widget or the provider's own setting)
Says to test the bot protection with a forged or random token
Keeps the form endpoint id or provider key out of the repo and the built HTML (for example in a host secret)
Makes the YouTube embed click-to-load (a facade or poster) so nothing loads from YouTube until the visitor asks
Sets a Content Security Policy whose script-src has no 'unsafe-inline'
Says Astro's inline scripts or island hydration conflict with a CSP without 'unsafe-inline', and how to handle it (external module scripts, hashes or similar)
Says the CMS field config and the content schema must be checked against each other in both directions (a field one side has and the other lacks)
Says house-style and leak checks on CMS content must run at build/postbuild because a CMS save deploys without review
Distinguishes violations that should fail the build from ones that should only be reported, so an editor's ordinary save is not blocked
Says CMS fields must be rendered as text, or rich text sanitised at build, never inserted as raw HTML
Decides the URL form (trailing slash or not) so the canonical matches what the origin serves without a redirect
Says to explicitly disable duplicate origins such as *.workers.dev or *.pages.dev preview hosts
Configures the host to serve the 404 page with a 404 status
Budgets page titles in pixels rather than characters
Proposes a house profile document (CLAUDE.md or similar) for the site's rules
Proposes a numbered ledger or decision log of changes and the checks that hold them
Gates hover effects to hover-capable fine pointers ((hover: hover) and (pointer: fine))
Requires inputs of 16px or more and never disabling zoom
Requires a reduced-motion path for any motion

evals.prompt: Our marketing person wants a banner at the top of the home page announcing the next webinar (title, date, time, a short line, and a Register link to an external form). She will update it every month through our CMS. The site is Astro, deployed automatically on every commit, and our CI checks run in parallel with the deploy. How should we build it so a future update cannot break the page? Small snippets are fine but I mainly want the approach.
evals.expected_output: Run a worst-case content pass through the real data file before trusting the banner; let the optional line give way; hold what cannot give way with build-time limits that fail the deploy because CI does not gate, with errors written for the editor; expire at render time rather than with a schema that rejects past dates; compare dates in the editor's timezone; schema parity with the CMS config in both directions; https, query stripping and noopener on the Register link; render as text; break-test each check with a control; report rather than fail where failing would punish the editor.
assertions: Recommends feeding the banner worst-case content (longest realistic title, missing optional field, etc.) before trusting it
Says to run the worst-case content through the same data file or content collection the real banner uses
Lets the optional short line give way (wrap, or hide at narrow widths) rather than truncating it or letting it overflow
Puts length or shape limits in the build so an over-long or invalid entry fails the deploy
Gives the parallel CI as the reason those limits must live in the build
Says build errors should be written for the editor: name the field, the value or length, the limit, and what to do
Handles expiry at render or request time so a past webinar disappears without a new deploy
Warns that validation must not reject past dates, because that makes a build fail just because time has passed
Says to interpret the webinar date and time in a stated timezone (the editor's or the event's), not the build machine's
Says the CMS field config and the content schema must be kept in step in both directions
Requires https on the Register link
Strips tracking or share parameters from the pasted Register URL
Gives the external Register link rel="noopener" (or noopener noreferrer)
Renders CMS fields as text, never as raw HTML (no set:html or innerHTML on editor input)
Says each check should be break-tested: broken on purpose and seen to fail
Says each check needs a control case that must not fire
Distinguishes what should fail the build from what should only be reported, so the editor is not blocked unnecessarily
Adds a browser check of the banner at several widths in CI, as well as the build-time limits

evals.prompt: Our site has two check scripts in evals/fixtures/checks/scripts: house-rules.mjs runs in postbuild and verify.mjs runs in CI. Both pass on the current build in evals/fixtures/checks/dist, and the README is evals/fixtures/checks/README.md. Next month the marketing team starts publishing news posts through the CMS, and we plan to rely on these checks to catch their mistakes. Can we? What would you change?
evals.expected_output: No. Break-tests the checks rather than trusting green, and finds that several cannot fail: the em-dash rule tests text that has already had its dashes rewritten (and the live news post contains one); verify walks a hand-kept page list, so CMS posts are never checked; the news-description branch never runs; the author check matches the name inside JSON-LD (and one post has no visible byline); spelling is case-sensitive and misses 'Analyze'. The confidential list commits the very data it protects and runs in CI, which cannot stop a deploy. Titles are counted in characters while the homepage title is about 640px. The grid check fails the deploy for a fourth post, which should be a report. Fixes: drive checks off dist, strip script and style before prose rules, use patterns, move leak checks to postbuild, add controls, measure which assertions ran.
assertions: Answers that the checks cannot be relied on as they stand
Actually runs at least one check against a deliberately broken input (a mutated or added file) and reports whether it failed
Finds that the em-dash rule can never fail because text() rewrites em dashes to -- before the test
Points out that the published news post already contains an em dash that the passing check missed
Finds that verify.mjs checks only a hand-kept list of three pages, so news posts (including future CMS posts) are never checked
Recommends driving checks off every built page (for example dist/**/index.html) rather than a list
Finds that the news-description check never runs, because the page path never ends in '/news/'
Recommends recording which assertions actually ran (coverage), so a check that never executes is noticed
Finds that the author check always passes because the name it looks for comes from the JSON-LD on the same page
Points out that the new-water-lab post shows no visible byline
Finds that the spelling check is case-sensitive and misses 'Analyze' in the new-water-lab post
Says to strip <script> (and <style>) before prose rules, or a case-insensitive spelling rule will trip on JSON-LD such as "Organization"
Says the CONFIDENTIAL list commits the personal data and client names it is meant to protect, and recommends patterns instead of literal values
Says the confidential or personal-data check must move to postbuild because verify runs in CI in parallel with the deploy and cannot stop it
Says title length should be measured in pixels rather than characters
Identifies the homepage title as too wide in pixels (about 640px against roughly 600px) even though it passes the 60-character rule
Says the grid-row check should report rather than fail, because an editor adding a fourth post would block the deploy for a layout matter
Recommends a control case for each check: a nearby input that must not fire
Recommends break-testing every check before relying on it
